issues.description: The problem statement and template expect a Farm.singFarmSong() method, but the solution implements playFarmSong() instead of singFarmSong(). This naming/signature mismatch between solution and the specified API will confuse students (and cause references in Main or tests to fail) because the expected method name from the exercise is not present in the solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Keep the API name consistent: rename the solution's playFarmSong() method to singFarmSong(), or add a public singFarmSong() wrapper in the solution that delegates to playFarmSong(). Alternatively, update the template/problem to use playFarmSong() if that name is preferred. Ensure Main and any tests use the same method name.

issues.description: The public method for playing the farm song is named singFarmSong() in the problem statement and the template, but the solution implementation exposes it as playFarmSong(). This naming divergence refers to the same conceptual operation (having the Farm perform the song) and can confuse students when mapping the required API to the reference solution or when attempting to run the commented examples in Main.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the public method name consistent across artifacts. Prefer renaming the solution method playFarmSong() to singFarmSong() so it matches the problem statement and template (or alternatively rename the template and problem references to playFarmSong()). Update any example usages (e.g., commented code in Main) accordingly.
